study_identification_part.si4_title: Characterizing the heterogeneity of neurodegenerative diseases through EEG normative modeling

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Use EEG-based normative modeling to chart age-related trajectories of spectral power and source-level functional connectivity in healthy adults over 40, and quantify individual-level deviations in Parkinson's disease (PD) and Alzheimer's disease (AD) and their clinical relevance.

rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.reason: Detailed preprocessing and feature computation steps are provided in Methods.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Deviations correlate with clinical severity: PD deviations vs UPDRS (rho = 0.24, p = 0.025); AD deviations vs MMSE (rho = -0.26, p = 0.01).
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: ~30% of patients show spectral deviations; ~80% show source connectivity deviations; spatial overlap among deviants ≤60% (spectral) and ≤25% (connectivity); deviations associate with worse UPDRS (PD) and lower MMSE (AD).
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Normative modeling of EEG spectral power and source-level connectivity reveals marked heterogeneity in PD and AD. Approximately 30% of patients exhibit spectral deviations while about 80% show connectivity deviations. Spatial overlap of deviant features is limited (≤60% for spectral, ≤25% for connectivity), indicating individualized deviation patterns. LOSO analyses show robust normative trajectories (r > 0.88/0.90). Deviations correlate with clinical scales (UPDRS, MMSE).
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: EEG deviation maps may enrich individualized clinical assessment in Precision Neurology by capturing patient-specific EEG abnormalities beyond group averages.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: Heterogeneous EEG systems and protocols not harmonized; downsampling to 19-channel montage may lose information; optimal channel count for reliable source networks uncertain; variable sample sizes across datasets; fixed frequency bands used instead of individualized alpha frequency; recommend advanced harmonization (e.g., ComBat family) and inclusion of environmental covariates in future work.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: Data aggregated from 14 clinical units; full dataset/site details, demographics, systems, and criteria are provided in Supplementary Data 1. Dataset 3 (BASEL) was preprocessed per prior publications (refs. 69–71).
